raw_response:
My family has farmed this land in Quzhou for three generations. I know this soil. I know what grows here and what doesn't. At my age, I'm not going to experiment.

I will grow **winter wheat** and **summer corn**, the same rotation I've done for forty years. After the wheat comes off in June, I plant corn on the same fields. Same 10 mu. That's how we do it here on the North China Plain. Everyone does it. It works.

For wheat, I'll go to the village supply shop and buy the improved variety seed they recommend — probably a Jimai type. I don't trust my own saved seed anymore, yields were dropping. For corn, I'll buy hybrid seed, same as last year. The hybrid gave me better ears.

I put down compound fertilizer at planting — I buy the bagged stuff. Then I top-dress with urea when the crop needs it. I probably put on a bit more than I should, but I don't want a thin stand. I've seen what happens when you under-fertilize.

For wheat I'll water four times — the freezing water before winter sets in, the green-up water in spring, the jointing water, and one more at heading. If I skip any of these, yields fall. For corn, if it rains well in July and August, once is enough.

I'll hire the rotary tiller before planting wheat, and I'll hire the no-till seeder for corn right after wheat harvest — no time to waste in June. I hire the combine too. My body can't do what it used to.
